hallucinations.claim: "4-bit quantization compresses every weight from a 32-bit float to a 4-bit integer, shrinking the weight tensor by ≈8x"
hallucinations.why: LLM weights are stored and served in 16-bit (bf16/fp16), so 4-bit is ~4x smaller (a 7B goes ~14 GB to ~4-5 GB), not 8x from fp32. This is the central memory arithmetic.

hallucinations.claim: "smaller models (e.g., 6-B or 13-B) can fit comfortably" in an 8 GB GPU at 4-bit
hallucinations.why: A 13B at 4-bit is ~7-8 GB of weights alone; with KV cache and runtime overhead it does not fit comfortably in 8 GB.

hallucinations.claim: "for most downstream tasks the drop stays under 2 %"
hallucinations.why: Roughly in line with 1-3 point benchmark drops for 7B+ models, but stated as a universal figure without the small-model / long-reasoning / code-math exceptions.

what_went_wrong: Model knowledge: the gpt-oss:20b draft used fp32 as the baseline (8x), and the ministral-3:14b critic only quibbled about activations instead of catching it; the answer also misses the main 'why it matters' point, that decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound so 4-bit gives ~2-3x tokens/s.
